lineage: Assessed to reuse Hive ransomware source code (Rust encryptor with substantial Hive overlap); announced shutdown in July 2025 with operators pivoting to the extortion-only 'World Leaks' brand
summary: Hunters International emerged in October 2023 using a Rust encryptor that shares much of its code with the disrupted Hive operation. Intrusions combined exploitation of exposed services (including an Oracle WebLogic debug port) with targeted malvertising of IT administrators via SharpRhino, a signed C# RAT disguised as Angry IP Scanner. Post-compromise tradecraft relied on Cobalt Strike, Impacket, Plink tunnelling, AnyDesk/TeamViewer and RDP, with registry-hive and NTDS credential theft and data theft to MEGA before encryption. In 2025 the group announced closure and its operators shifted to World Leaks, a data-theft-only extortion brand.

chain.procedure: Exploits an internet-exposed Oracle WebLogic server via its debug port (TCP 8453, CVE-2020-14644) to gain code execution on the perimeter host.
chain.noAtomicReason: Exploitation of an internet-facing service is not reproducible with a local Windows atomic; validate with perimeter/WAF and application logs instead.

chain.procedure: IT administrators are lured (typosquatted Angry IP Scanner domain) into running a signed NSIS installer that drops the SharpRhino C# RAT.

atomics.note: Executes a downloaded potentially-unwanted application; stands in for the user running a trojanised admin-tool installer.

chain.techniqueName: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
chain.procedure: SharpRhino establishes persistence by modifying the Windows Registry Run key and creating a shortcut (LNK) so the RAT relaunches at logon.

atomics.note: Run-key persistence as reported for SharpRhino.

chain.procedure: PowerShell is used post-compromise (SharpRhino tasking and on the WebLogic host) to pull down additional tooling such as Cobalt Strike.

chain.procedure: Plink (PuTTY) SSH tunnels expose internal RDP to attacker infrastructure.
